name: Indian Ocean South Equatorial Undercurrent
scope: Declared 60-105 E March-May subsurface geographic reach. Approximate source longitude limits and west/east latitude context guide an OSW connecting path; not diagnosed whole-current endpoints. Surface SEC/SECC, equatorial EUC, ridge circulation loops and western/eastern extensions excluded.
layer: BRAN2020 representative isopycnal context 27.9-28.7 sigma0. Source converts this to roughly 300-420 m at the mooring only; not a fixed-depth route throughout the basin.
time_convention: March-May monthly climatological context from 2001-2018 BRAN2020. Not a dated observed axis, annual geometry or a reconstruction of the anomalous 2020 current.
source_locator: Sections 2 and 3; Figure 2b caption: BRAN monthly climatology, density-layer context and approximate 60-105 E reach shifting from 8 S to 10 S. Figure 3 core threshold is a separate diagnostic.
source_citation: Chen, Han, Zu, Chu and Chen (2022), The Deep-Penetrating South Equatorial Undercurrent in the Tropical South Indian Ocean, Geophysical Research Letters 49, e2022GL098163, doi:10.1029/2022GL098163.
source_license: Attributed factual geography; no source figure, velocity field or model array copied. No open figure-reuse license inferred.
coordinate_selection: Rounded 60 E, 8 S and 105 E, 10 S follow approximate prose context. OSW interpolates middle vertices; no dotted core center or bathymetric contour traced. Alternative middle latitude bends and endpoint shifts test editorial drawing choices, not source position errors.

alternative_routes.interpretation: OSW middle-latitude drawing sensitivity; not a month, current edge or diagnosed velocity core.

scenario_rule: Three declared shapes with fixed longitude gates and independent start/end latitude offsets -0.25/0/+0.25 degrees: 27 editorial cases. Not seasonal minima/maxima, uncertainty or width bounds.
remaining_gates: Extract compatible BRAN density-layer core geometry and review ridge-scale continuity before interpreting the connecting line as an axis.
